title: Running total in place
starter:
%b  = buffer 3 dtype=i32 slot=0 data=[1 2 3]
# In place: b[1] = b[0] + b[1], then b[2] = (the NEW b[1]) + b[2].
%e0 = shrink %b 0 shape=[]
%e1 = shrink %b 1 shape=[]
%e2 = shrink %b 2 shape=[]
%a  = load %e0
%c  = load %e1
%n1 = add %a %c
%s1 = store %e1 %n1
%b1 = after %b %s1
%d  = load %e2
%n2 = add %c %d
%f2 = shrink %b1 2 shape=[]
%s2 = store %f2 %n2
%b2 = after %b1 %s2
hints: The starter's answer for `[1 2 3]` is `[1 3 5]`. Which value of b[1] did it add to b[2]?
`%c` was loaded from version `%b`, before the first store. The new b[1] lives in version `%b1`.
Either add `%n1` (the value you just stored) to `%d`, or load b[1] again from `shrink %b1 1 shape=[]`.
explain: The bug reads the old b[1] from version `%b`. The fix uses the new value, either `%n1` directly or a load from version `%b1`. A load names the version it reads, which is how the graph says "before" or "after" a store without any statement order.
